direction.comments: The direction on a macro and micro scale combines elements from Trailer Park Boys and Jackass to create a fun and entertaining experience; Storytelling is good, as the movie makes you feel invested in the story as they paint each character's personal attachment

performance.comments: Really goes full Trailer Park Boys as really feels like he is enjoying himself as he tries to make the movie and keep his friend's legacy alive; has good comedic timing and has good chemistry with the cast
Plays his character pretty well and establishes good chemistry with Quinn
Plays her character well and acts as the sane glue for the group
Feels like a weird character that doesn't really suit his voice, but he makes it is own as you can tell he's having fun making this movie

cast.comments: The cast is pretty small but everyone feels like they are having fun and working as a team to help move this story forward and keep you entertained

story.comments: The concept follows this group of Canadian degenerates making a movie to honor their stunt-buddy friend, resulting in a film that feels as if Trailer Park Boys and Jackass had a baby; The plot structure is quite linear, with the end of the movie being the film they created; Character writing is surprisingly good, as each character has their own motive for making this movie, proving they are more than just dunces whom the town hates

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is very Canadian and very funny, as this movie does not stop making jokes that hit surprisingly well; There surprisingly is a decent amount of symbolism, as the movie touches on the doubt these characters have as they grieve the loss of their friend and whether or not they should just grow up and move on; Foreshadowing is present

cinematography.comments: The cinematography feels very low-budget and DIY, and the camcorder shots really add to how these degenerates are trying to make this makeshift movie with absolutely no money

editing.comments: The editing helps add to this DIY, low-budget feel

sound.comments: The sound helps paint the stunts and action sequences for this movie and helps bring to life the old technology they are using

visual_effects.comments: A lot of practical stunts make this movie feel like a Canadian version of Jackass, which is good given how low the budget for this movie is

production_design.comments: The production design is basically middle-of-nowhere Canada as they try to recreate Trailer Park Boys

costumes.comments: The costumes definitely paint these characters in an interesting light

review.pacing: The pacing is right, as the movie does not feel too fast or slow, since the jokes and the action really move this story forward
review.climax: The climax is good, as it helps culminate the film they are making and provides closure for all the characters' journeys
review.tone: The tone is basically as if Trailer Park Boys and Jackass had a baby, all with a low-budget, DIY feel
review.final_notes: I saw the world premiere at SXSW
review.overall: Overall, 'Crash Land' is basically as if Trailer Park Boys and Jackass had a baby, as they essentially made a DIY, low-budget comedy that is duct-taped together by its degenerate comedy and degenerate stunts, creating such a fun time you won't forget
